archives.name: root-none
archives.description: Root directory only, internal compression none.

archives.name: root-gzip
archives.description: Same tiles as root-none; root directory and metadata gzip-compressed (stored deflate blocks).

archives.name: leaves-gzip
archives.description: Root directory holds only two leaf entries; every tile is found through a gzip leaf directory. z0-z3 plus the spec example 12/3423/1763 (tile id 19078479). A 27812-byte tile at id 2 puts later tile data past the first 16 KiB.

archives.name: exact-8192
archives.description: Exactly 8192 bytes, root directory only, gzip internal compression. The file ends with the last tile byte (no padding), so the 16 KiB opening request bytes=0-16383 is answered with the whole archive, tile data included (Content-Range: bytes 0-8191/8192).

archives.name: bad-magic
archives.description: root-none with the first magic byte changed from 'P' to 'X'.

archives.name: bad-version
archives.description: root-none with the spec version byte (offset 7) changed from 3 to 4.

archives.name: truncated-header
archives.description: root-none cut to its first 126 bytes, one byte short of the 127-byte header.

archives.name: truncated-file
archives.description: root-none with its final byte removed (904 of 905 bytes kept); the header still declares the original tile data length, so tile data ends 1 byte past the end of the file.

archives.name: truncated-directory
archives.description: root-none with the header's root directory length reduced from 26 to 25 bytes, so the final offset varint of the root directory runs off its end.

archives.name: varint-overflow
archives.description: root-none with the first 10 bytes of the root directory replaced by ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 02: the entry-count varint's 10th byte is above 1, so the value needs more than 64 bits.

archives.name: section-overflow
archives.description: root-none with the header's metadata offset set to 2^64-10; offset + length (2^64-10 + 152) wraps around 2^64 to 142, which a check without overflow detection would accept as inside the 905-byte file.

archives.name: root-beyond-16k
archives.description: root-none with 16257 zero bytes inserted after the header and all section offsets shifted, so the root directory starts at byte 16384, outside the first 16384 bytes.

archives.name: empty-directory
archives.description: root-none with the root directory's entry-count varint changed from 6 to 0.

archives.name: too-many-entries
archives.description: root-none with the first 6 bytes of the root directory replaced by the varint 2^40 (80 80 80 80 80 20): the 26-byte directory claims 1099511627776 entries.

archives.name: zero-length-entry
archives.description: root-none with the length of the last root entry (tile id 20) changed from 120 to 0.

archives.name: entry-out-of-bounds
archives.description: root-none with the length of the last root entry (tile id 20, tile data offset 480) changed from 120 to 121, so it ends 1 byte past the 600-byte tile data section.

archives.name: leaf-cycle
archives.description: leaves-gzip with the second leaf directory replaced by a gzip leaf directory holding one leaf entry that points at itself (same leaf offset and length); the root entry's length is updated to match. Following it never reaches a tile.

archives.name: decompression-bomb
archives.description: root-gzip with the root directory replaced by a 6677-byte gzip member (one fixed-Huffman block: literal 0, then 4096 length-258 distance-1 matches) that inflates to 1056769 zero bytes, more than the 1 MiB limit.

archives.name: unknown-compression
archives.description: root-none with the internal compression byte (offset 97) changed from 1 (none) to 7, a value the spec does not define.

archives.name: invalid-metadata
archives.description: root-none with the metadata replaced by the JSON array [1,2] (valid JSON, but not an object); later sections are shifted.

archives.name: unsupported-zstd
archives.description: root-none built with internal compression zstd (4): the root directory and metadata are zstd frames of raw (uncompressed) blocks. Valid PMTiles; pmtiles-lab does not decode zstd.

mvt_corpus.name: mvt-points
mvt_corpus.description: One original MVT tileset, packaged as PMTiles v3 and MBTiles 1.3 with identical gzip tile bytes. Expected features come from the corpus source, not from either file.
mvt_corpus.content_rights: Original synthetic data written for this repository (names are the ICAO spelling alphabet, positions are arbitrary tile coordinates). No map data or third-party content. Apache-2.0, see LICENSE and NOTICE.
mvt_corpus.generator_inputs: internal/fixtures/mvtcorpus.go (tiles and features), mvt.go (MVT 2.1 encoder), sqlite.go (SQLite 3 file writer), encode.go (stored-block gzip). Go standard library only; no third-party code or data.

vector_layers.description: Labelled points: name (string) and rank (unsigned integer).

files.description: PMTiles v3, tile type mvt, tile compression gzip, internal compression gzip; root directory holds only leaf entries (3 leaves).
MBTiles 1.3 (SQLite 3, application_id 0x4d504258): metadata format pbf with a json vector_layers row; tiles with TMS tile_row; unique tile_index.

tiles.purpose: north-west z1 tile; its TMS mirror 1/0/1 is absent
south-east z1 tile with two features
top row; its TMS mirror 2/1/3 is absent
absent; tile id 21, inside the second leaf directory's range
z3 tile in the last leaf directory

mbtiles_archives.name: tiles-view
mbtiles_archives.change: tiles is a view over map (zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row, tile_id) joined with images (tile_id, tile_data), the layout mbutil writes; unique indexes map_index and images_id replace tile_index
mbtiles_archives.description: The corpus tiles, read through a view named tiles. A reader must query tiles by name and not require a table; every corpus coordinate reads as in mvt_corpus.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md), Database: "SQLite views that produce compatible results MAY be used instead."

mbtiles_archives.name: wal-mode
mbtiles_archives.change: header bytes 18 and 19 (file format write and read versions) set to 2, WAL mode; no -wal file, as after a full checkpoint
mbtiles_archives.description: A WAL-mode database with every change in the main file. A reader must read every corpus tile. SQLite may create the -wal and -shm files beside it when it opens it, even read-only; open a copy if that directory must not change.

validity.source: SQLite file format 1.3.3: versions 2 mean WAL (SQLite 3.7.0 or later); MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "Tilesets SHALL be valid SQLite databases of version 3.0.0 or higher."

mbtiles_archives.name: not-sqlite
mbtiles_archives.change: first byte of the header string "SQLite format 3\0" changed from S to X
mbtiles_archives.description: Not an SQLite database. A reader must refuse it at open.

validity.source: SQLite file format 1.3.1: every database file starts with "SQLite format 3\0"; MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "Tilesets SHALL be valid SQLite databases".

mbtiles_archives.name: empty-file
mbtiles_archives.description: SQLite opens a 0-byte file as an empty database, so the file has no tables. A reader must refuse it at open, never serve a tileset with every tile absent.

validity.source: SQLite opens a 0-byte file as an empty database; MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "The database MUST contain a table or view named metadata" and "a table named tiles".

mbtiles_archives.name: truncated
mbtiles_archives.change: file cut after page 3 of 4 (12288 bytes); the header still says 4 pages and the schema names page 4 as the root of tile_index
mbtiles_archives.description: A truncated database. A reader must refuse it at open (SQLite reports "database disk image is malformed" on the first query).

validity.source: SQLite file format 1.3.7: the in-header size (4 pages) is valid because the change counter equals version-valid-for, and the file holds 3 pages; MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "Tilesets SHALL be valid SQLite databases".

mbtiles_archives.name: no-metadata-table
mbtiles_archives.description: No name, format or vector_layers. A reader must refuse it at open.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "The database MUST contain a table or view named metadata."

mbtiles_archives.name: no-tiles-table
mbtiles_archives.change: tiles table and its tile_index removed
mbtiles_archives.description: Metadata without tiles. A reader must refuse it at open, never serve every tile as absent or fail tile by tile.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "The database MUST contain a table named tiles."

mbtiles_archives.name: wrong-format
mbtiles_archives.change: metadata format pbf changed to png; tiles unchanged (gzip MVT)
mbtiles_archives.description: The format row does not describe the tiles. A vector tile reader must refuse it at open, not decode tiles labelled png.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): format is "The file format of the tile data"; the tile data is gzip-compressed MVT, which is pbf.

mbtiles_archives.name: no-vector-layers
mbtiles_archives.description: A pbf tileset without layer metadata. A tolerant reader opens it and reads every tile as in mvt_corpus; a reader that needs vector_layers (for example to write TileJSON, which requires it) refuses it at open.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "If the format is pbf, the metadata table MUST contain this row: json".

mbtiles_archives.name: zoom-range-mismatch
mbtiles_archives.change: metadata maxzoom 3 changed to 2; the z3 row 3/5/2 is kept
mbtiles_archives.description: Metadata says the tileset ends at z2 but a z3 tile exists. A reader may serve 3/5/2 or treat it as outside the tileset; every other tile reads as in mvt_corpus.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): the vector_layers maxzoom is 3, and "the maxzoom MUST be less than or equal to the tileset's maxzoom"; maxzoom is "The highest zoom level for which the tileset provides data".

mbtiles_archives.name: corrupt-gzip
mbtiles_archives.change: 1/1/1 tile_data cut to the first half of its gzip member (no trailer)
mbtiles_archives.description: One tile with a truncated gzip stream. A reader must report an error for 1/1/1, never partial features, an empty tile or absent, and read the other tiles.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "pbf as a format refers to gzip-compressed vector tile data"; the 1/1/1 member is incomplete (RFC 1952).

mbtiles_archives.name: mixed-gzip
mbtiles_archives.change: 2/1/0 tile_data stored as the plain MVT; every other tile gzip
mbtiles_archives.description: One uncompressed tile in a pbf tileset. A reader may see that the gzip magic is missing (no MVT starts with 0x1f) and decode it, or report an error; every other tile reads as in mvt_corpus.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "pbf as a format refers to gzip-compressed vector tile data".

tiles.purpose: plain MVT in a gzip tileset

mbtiles_archives.name: decompression-bomb
mbtiles_archives.change: 0/0/0 tile_data is one 65,568-byte gzip member that inflates to 67,633,153 zero bytes (64.5 MiB + 1), stored on 16 overflow pages
mbtiles_archives.description: A decompression bomb: a valid gzip member (one dynamic-Huffman block, about 1031:1, correct CRC-32 and ISIZE) whose content is not an MVT. A reader must stop at its own decompressed-size limit, report an error for 0/0/0 in bounded memory, and read the other tiles.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md): "pbf as a format refers to gzip-compressed vector tile data in Mapbox Vector Tile format"; the inflated content is zero bytes, not a protobuf message (field number 0 is not valid).

mbtiles_archives.name: duplicate-rows
mbtiles_archives.change: unique tile_index replaced by a non-unique index; an extra row at 1/0/0 (tile_row 1) holding 1/1/1's tile_data, inserted first (rowid 1)
mbtiles_archives.description: Two rows for one coordinate. A reader should report an error for 1/0/0; one that takes the first row gets 1/1/1's features, one that takes the last gets 1/0/0's.

validity.source: MBTiles 1.3 (github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec 682fed79, 1.3/spec.md) has no rule against two rows at one coordinate; the unique tile_index is optional ("The database MAY contain an index for efficient access to this table").

tiles.purpose: two rows; the first holds 1/1/1's tile
